newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan should focus on implementing budget - PM.
newsitem.headline: Japan should focus on implementing budget - PM.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Friday the government should concentrate on the smooth and steady implementation of the main state budget for this fiscal year ending March 31.
"At the moment, the important thing is implement the 1996/97 (main) state budget smoothly and various government policies," Hashimoto said.
He added that the government would keep a watch over economic conditions.
Japan's economy was continuing to recover gradually and demand led by the private-sector was growing steadily, he said. However, employment conditions remained severe, he said.
Hashimoto said Japan would have to come up with a supplementary budget this fiscal year anyway to cover necessary costs, such as reconstruction after the January 1995 Kobe earthquake.
Discussions on whether additional public works spending should be included in the extra budget should take place without a particular figure in mind, Hashimoto said.
Politicians from Hashimoto's Liberal Democratic Party have called for a supplementary budget worth a total of five trillion yen, including public works spending.
